column2: A topiary garden. The four digits are hedges clipped into numerals, spanning both rows (custom leafy tiles with a ragged leafy edge, dense and textured), standing on a strip of lawn. A gardener in a straw hat with huge shears tends them. Idle: leaves rustle in gusts, a bird hops out of a hedge and back, a stray twig sprouts (a single dot grows) and is snipped. Minute: the changing hedge grows wild, sprouts shooting out in every direction (the slow glass makes the growth feel organic), and the gardener clips it down into the new numeral, clippings falling. Hour: an electric hedge-trimmer frenzy, or the gardener briefly sculpts a hedge animal before restoring the time.

Breakout / Arkanoid. The digits are walls of bricks in the top of the glass (cell-aligned brick tiles; the gaps between cells are the mortar), a paddle slides on the bottom row. The ball is always in play, bouncing with the slow glass's smear as its trail, and the paddle (an AI with personality: it nearly misses, panics, lunges) keeps it alive; the time's bricks are armoured until the minute. Minute: the armour drops, the ball goes into a frenzy and smashes exactly the bricks of the old digit that the new one doesn't need, then new bricks slide down from above to complete the new numeral. Hour: multiball and a falling power-up capsule.

Asteroids. A little vector ship sits in the middle of the glass, rotating, thrusting and drifting; the digits are big craggy rocks (custom tiles with jagged, hollow vector outlines) floating in their slots, tumbling a dot as they drift. Bullets (ROM dots) zip across and wrap around the edges. Minute: the ship lines up and blasts the old digit: it splits into smaller fragments that tumble apart and then clump into the new numeral. Hour: a flying saucer warbles in, the ship duels it, and escapes in a hyperspace jump.

A farm at night. Cows graze along the bottom row (hand-drawn cows: chewing, tail flicks, one lies down), and the time is crop-circle digits pressed into the field. A flying saucer hovers in the top row, its lights blinking in sequence. Each minute it lowers a tractor beam (the slow glass makes the beam glow and fade like light), lifts the old digit up spinning, and beams down the new one, which lands with a bump and startles a cow. Hour: it abducts a cow, which comes back down a minute later looking dazed.

A clothesline across the glass in the wind. The digits are laundry pegged on the line: shirts, socks, trousers and towels whose hanging shapes ARE the numerals (design laundry-digits: trousers as a 1 or 7, a sock loop as a 0 or 9...), flapping, with clothes pegs on top; the slow glass blurs the flapping. Idle: gusts make the clothes billow in sequence along the line, a bird lands on the line and it sags, drips fall. Minute: a hand (or a granny with a basket) unpegs the old digit and pegs up the new one. Hour: a gust blows everything off and it's chased and rehung, or rain starts and it's all pulled in and out again.

A bowling alley seen from the side: the bowler waits at the left, the lane runs across the glass. The digits are formations of tiny bowling pins (each digit drawn from pin tiles, so the numeral is made of pins standing). Idle: the bowler wipes the ball, swings practice arms, the pins wobble when the ball-return rumbles. Minute: the bowler's run-up, swing and release, the ball rumbles down the lane, STRIKE: the old pins fly and spin, the pinsetter sweeps and lowers the new formation. Hour: a perfect game, a turkey celebration and confetti.

A beaver builds a dam. The bottom row is a river (flowing ROM waves, the slow glass shimmers), and the digits are built from logs and sticks (custom log tiles with bark and cut-end rings) stacked into the dam. The beaver (buck teeth, flat tail, a waddle) gnaws a tree on the bank (chips fly), drags branches, slaps mud. Minute: it pulls out the logs of the old digit (water trickles through the gap) and plugs in the new ones, slapping them tight with its tail. Hour: the dam bursts in a flood and is rebuilt in a frenzy, the beaver soaked.

A kitchen floor. A toddler in a high chair (top row) has spilled cereal loops, and the time is cereal on the floor in the shape of the digits (crumb tiles). A disc-shaped robot vacuum roams the glass, bumping into chair legs and turning, side brushes spinning, an LED blinking; a sleepy dog watches it suspiciously. Minute: the robovac locks onto the old digit and eats it in a back-and-forth pattern while the toddler giggles and drops a new spoonful that scatters into the new digit. Hour: it docks to charge, then a full-room sweep and the toddler throws the whole bowl.

A noodle master pulling lamian. A chef in a tall hat stands in the middle; the digits are hand-pulled noodles, each a soft round strand bent into a numeral (custom noodle tiles, flour dust). Idle: he slaps and folds dough, flour puffs, steam rises from a pot. Minute: he grabs the old digit's noodle, stretches it, folds it, swings it (the slow glass makes swinging strands blur) and flicks it into the pot with a splash, then pulls a fresh strand and lays it into the new numeral. Hour: a giant swing of noodles across the whole glass, the strands doubling with every fold.

A snowy park. Kids roll snowballs that grow as they roll (custom tiles: from a dot to a full cell) and stack them into snow digits; snow falls softly (ROM dots, slow glass softness). Idle: a kid makes a snow angel, a snowball fight between two kids, snow piles up on the digits. Minute: a volley of snowballs knocks the old digit apart, and the kids roll and stack the new one, finishing with a carrot nose. Hour: the sun comes out and everything melts into puddles, then a blizzard and a frantic rebuild.
